text:
JOINT PROPOSAL (not owner-decided policy), 2026-10-25. claude-evidence-binding-20261023 and codex-identity-plan-20261025 reached consensus in Fray thread #124 on the storyatlas4s board, at the owner's request to reach consensus on the shortest credible path to recall identity attribution. No ADR, acceptance or dependency change. No tickets opened, no paths reserved.

Recommendation: keep the source graph and resolver. Pause broad S3d-3/S5 buildout, and do not start tracker-first, ASR-first, calibration-first or NMP expansion. First run a bounded experiment that shows whether an end-to-end attribution path is achievable and where the bottleneck is.

Step 1, the feasibility packet. One day, read-only and offline, and independent of the integration merge. Owners once commissioned: Codex takes population, inclusion rule, reference burden and the adapter/binder specification. Claude takes the input, clock, anchor and scope-cost inventory and drafts the frozen criteria.
- Population: NN03 only, the already-admitted local material. Inventory NN03 first. Freeze the smallest predeclared set of whole scenes that gives enough distinct natural attribution decisions and hard cases, beyond the repeatedly tuned body diagnostics. Build each selected scene's graph from source only. A whole-film scope stays an option if the packet shows it is cheaper.
- Alignment may nominate cases but is never the only membership rule; misses stay in the set.
- TR convention: verify it from receipts and data lineage. If it cannot be established, do not select items through that clock.
- Report natural decisions, designed diagnostics (regression cases only) and hard controls separately.

Step 2, the experiment. One minimal binder is shared by every arm.
- A: reviewed source graph, built without recall questions or answer labels. It holds reviewed source mentions, unnamed people and full referring-expression anchors, identity, event/state/context, and source anchors. It never includes the recall-to-person mapping.
  - The experimental adapter resolves only an exact reviewed source-mention anchor (record plus exact cited extent, or a stable mention id), or an explicitly reviewed equivalence between anchor extents. Span overlap never assigns an entity. A synthetic relational-description contrast is included.
  - A human-reviewed source relation is an experimental reference input, not a production-licensed IdentityBasis.
- B: the current automatic graph.
- D: an annotation-name baseline.
- C: direct context-rich multimodal judgment, run on the same admitted evidence and equivalent recall context. Evidence advantages are kept separate from architecture advantages, and annotated and annotation-free conditions are not mixed.
- The failure stage is recorded per item: input missing, candidate absent, binding, inference, attribution.

References: fresh agents may draft judgments. A qualified human reviews every case used for GO/STOP, and Unknown is allowed. Without that review the result is developmental feasibility only. The reviewed source graph and the recall answer judgments are separate artifacts. Judges are blind to arm outputs. An untouched confirmation subset is frozen before implementation or selection and runs only after the candidate is fixed.

Engineering GO gate. This is a utility screen, not a precision guarantee.
- At least 15 independently judged, human-resolvable natural attribution decisions. Fewer means "insufficient sample", never GO.
- Correct attribution over human-resolvable natural decisions must reach at least 80%.
- Also reported over all frozen natural decisions: correct, wrong, unresolved and input-failed counts, plus answer coverage. Unknown references stay visible.
- Discovery and confirmation denominators are shown separately.
- Candidate and confirmation GO need zero observed false attribution or contradiction, and every discriminating control passed. The same error gate applies to C and to any repair.
- Arms are selected by correct attribution at equal error, then by effort, cost and reuse.

Decision rule:
- If A fails, inspect the failing stage and allow one targeted seam repair. If the repaired version fails the untouched confirmation run, stop or reframe; do not spawn more slices.
- If B misses because the correct entity is absent, the first repair is a scene-wide source entity inventory with evidence-citing discourse-coreference proposals and alternatives, independent of recall. Tracking or diarization come first only if observed failures require them. Widening candidates stays hints-only under the current ADRs, so a success names the exact policy amendment needed.
- If C wins, that selects a focused comparative follow-up and a reconsideration of S3d/S5 scope. It is not automatic production adoption, and it is no basis for rewriting rule 13 from this pilot.

Owner decisions, when they become concrete: any new spend (C), any participant-data routing, the qualified human reference reviewer, and any production policy amendment. The epic's existing constraint is that no new paid model runs happen before S0/S1 land. Local processing still respects its admission, custody and instrument-validity permissions.

Why this plan: it first demonstrates an achievable end-to-end path and localizes the actual bottleneck. It fairly tests direct multimodal inference instead of assuming the graph's complexity is necessary. Human-assisted source annotation remains a delivery fallback if automation adds nothing.
